motion.name: cinematic-dress-sequence
motion.value: 180 canvas frames at 24 fps, scrubbed reversibly by native scroll; separate portrait sequence at 600px and below
motion.purpose: Completed original landscape and portrait films replace the rejected five-cutout assembly. Trim the first 7.5 seconds before reversal to preserve the complete gown endpoint. Continuous rendered cloth, a locked camera, and no added desktop zoom establish the visual motion. Reduced motion uses a finished-gown still. Local browser results and limits: docs/review/sues-tailor/cinematic/README.md. Physical-phone performance and visual parity are not established; technical checks do not imply user acceptance.

narrative.overview: Scoped to Sue’s Tailor Shop at /demo/sues-tailor. The feminine neighborhood boutique direction remains. The five-cutout hero is REJECTED and obsolete; its working transforms and captures are not visual acceptance. Completed original landscape and portrait garment films now supply 180-frame scroll-controlled canvas sequences. Source contact sheets show continuous cloth bending and finished-gown endpoints; local browser results and limits are recorded in docs/review/sues-tailor/cinematic/README.md. The opening portrait composition slightly clips outer fabric; the completed gown fits. Physical-phone performance and visual parity are not established, and technical checks do not imply user acceptance. Appointment controls must remain accessible, the local demo form sends or books nothing, and illustrative gown imagery establishes no custom dressmaking service.
keyCharacteristics: A continuous cinematic garment sequence with completed landscape and native portrait media; preserve the fine needle-and-thread mark. The former five transparent cutouts are rejected.
A dark plum hero with amber light and cream type leads into warm ivory, soft blush surfaces, deep burgundy, and restrained copper-brown accents.
Expressive serif headings paired with small, calm sans-serif utility text.
Open sections and ruled service rows, with subtle motion tied to interaction.
dos: Do preserve the feminine dress-focused boutique direction, serif and sans-serif pairing, square controls, and fine tailoring mark.
Do keep the fitting request, call action, and appointment-only language easy to find on narrow screens.
Do preserve the illustrative image disclosure and the user-requested absence of visible Wallace Shift attribution.
Do visually assess the replacement against the verified reference and keep technical checks separate from user acceptance.
donts: Don't represent the generated dress stages as the shop's actual work or promise custom gown creation.
Don't imply the local preview sends an appointment request or reserves a fitting.
Don't turn the review selector into an automatic carousel or add motion that ignores reduced-motion preferences.
Don't present the rejected cutout proposal or its historical captures as the accepted design direction.
